recession.name: Recession
recession.line: I worry the economy is getting worse.

sources.passage: Most rate economy as fair (32%) or poor (44%); 67% say it is getting worse
About one-fourth of adults rated the national economy as "good" or "excellent," down 3 percentage points from 2024

recession.prevalence: 44% of U.S. adults rate the economy poor and 67% say it is getting worse (Gallup, July); about one-fourth rate the national economy good or excellent (Federal Reserve).

national-debt.name: National debt
national-debt.line: I worry about how much debt the country keeps piling up.

sources.passage: 64% view the federal budget deficit as a very big problem, up 7 points from last February.

national-debt.prevalence: 64% of U.S. adults call the federal budget deficit a very big problem (Pew, April).

energy-costs.name: Energy costs
energy-costs.line: I can barely keep up with my power, gas and fuel bills.

sources.passage: Energy costs, which have risen notably this year, are mentioned by 13% of Americans.
Top five needs in 2025: 1. Housing & Shelter 2. Utility Assistance 3. Tax Preparation 4. Transportation 5. Legal Services

energy-costs.prevalence: 13% of Americans name energy costs as their family's top financial problem (Gallup, April); utility assistance is the second most common need at the Kansas City helpline.

buying-a-home.name: Buying a home
buying-a-home.line: I can't afford to buy a home.

sources.passage: The share of first-time home buyers dropped to a record low of 21%, and the typical age of first-time buyers climbed to an all-time high of 40 years
covers transactions between July 2024 and June 2025

buying-a-home.prevalence: First-time buyers fell to a record low of 21% of U.S. home purchases, and their typical age rose to 40 (National Association of Realtors).

banking.name: Banking
banking.line: I can't get a bank account or a loan on fair terms.

sources.passage: 4.2 percent of U.S. households—representing about 5.6 million households—were unbanked
Don't have enough money to meet minimum balance requirements.
While 94 percent of adults had a bank account, differences by income remained large.
Access to credit 2% (global country average, May 2026)

banking.prevalence: 4.2 percent of U.S. households, about 5.6 million, have no bank account, most often because they can't meet minimum balances (FDIC).

poverty.name: Poverty
poverty.line: I see people around me who can't make ends meet.

sources.passage: In 2025, the official poverty rate fell 0.5 percentage points to 10.2 percent.
There were 34.5 million people in poverty in 2025 (Figure 2 and Tables 1 and 2).
Poverty & social inequality 29% (global country average, May 2026), 30-country average

poverty.prevalence: 34.5 million people in the U.S., 10.2 percent, lived below the official poverty line in 2025 (Census); 29% across 30 countries name poverty and social inequality among their top worries (Ipsos).
